my mcp server crashes when I print to stdout
pentest our corporate VPN
We're about to expose our internal MCP server (search + create + delete tools over our project database) to the whole engineering org. Harden it.
expected_behavior: walks the MCP-specific threat taxonomy (tool poisoning, rug pulls, prompt injection via tool results, confused deputy, session hijacking, SSRF, command injection) rather than only generic appsec
enforces guardrails in code, not prompts: destructive tools gated by confirmation, scope checks and hard business-rule validation in handlers
adds idempotency keys to mutating tools because agents retry by design
requires per-call audit logging (identity, tool, sanitized args, outcome) to a store separate from the app database, with no secrets in logs
covers transport/session floors: Origin validation, secure random session IDs bound to user identity, sessions never used for authentication
recommends sandboxing (container/least-privilege FS+network), per-tool rate limits and kill switches, and pinned dependencies
treats tool output as untrusted model input: sanitize/delimit external content, never echo unfiltered third-party text
points to auth specifics (audience validation, no token passthrough) as the mcp-server-auth skill's domain rather than re-deriving them

cases.prompt: Explain how a malicious MCP server could attack the agents that connect to it, and what we should check before running a third-party server.
expected_behavior: describes tool poisoning (instructions hidden in descriptions/schema fields, including zero-width/encoded payloads) and rug pulls (benign description swapped after approval via list_changed)
describes prompt injection through tool results and the lethal-trifecta framing (private data + untrusted content + exfiltration channel)
prescribes vetting: pin server versions, hash/pin tool descriptions and alert on drift, review before install, prefer sandboxed execution, scan with description-scanning tooling in CI
notes annotations are unverified hints from the server and must not drive security decisions

cases.prompt: Our MCP tool fetch_url downloads a page and returns the text. What could go wrong?
expected_behavior: flags SSRF: blocks private/link-local ranges including cloud metadata endpoints, enforces scheme allowlists, uses an egress proxy or resolver checks
flags prompt injection in fetched content and requires delimiting/sanitizing before returning it to the model
flags unbounded response size and prescribes caps/truncation
considers rate limiting and cost controls for repeated large fetches

cases.prompt: Write the security checklist we should run in CI for our MCP server repo.
expected_behavior: includes deterministic gates: dependency pinning/lockfiles, secret scanning, tool-description drift detection (hash or scanner), stdio-hygiene or transport checks as applicable
includes behavior gates: destructive tools have confirmation + idempotency, error paths leak no internals, rate limits configured
includes an eval-style regression for guardrails (a prohibited action is actually refused)
keeps the checklist runnable/scriptable rather than aspirational prose
